practice: Multiply numerators 2·3=6 and denominators x·5=5x. The original denominator excludes x=0.
Cancel the nonzero x and reduce 8/4=2. x=0 remains excluded.
30x/(45x²)=2/(3x), with x≠0 from the original denominator.
Factor x²−9=(x−3)(x+3). Cancel x−3 and x+2 only after recording original denominator restrictions.
Factor x²−4=(x−2)(x+2), x²−1=(x−1)(x+1). Cancel x+2 and x−1; keep all original exclusions.
Factor numerator (x+2)(x+3) and denominator (x−2)(x+2); every factor cancels where the original product is defined.
Multiply to get 36x²y²/(24xy), then reduce to 3xy/2. Both original denominators must be nonzero.
Use x²−16=(x−4)(x+4), cancel x and x+4, and simplify 6/2=3.
Factor x(x−5)/[(x−5)(x+5)] and multiply by (x+5)/x; all factors cancel on the original domain.
Factor (x+1)(x+2)/[(x−1)(x+1)] and cancel x+1 and x−1 against the second numerator.
Factor (x−2)²/[(x−2)(x+2)]; cancel one x−2 and x+2, leaving (x−2)/(x−1).
A student simplifies ((x²−6x+9)/(x²−9))((x+3)/(x−3)) to 1. Which x-values are excluded?
The simplification is 1 because (x−3)²/[(x−3)(x+3)]·(x+3)/(x−3)=1, but original denominators exclude ±3.
Factor (x+5)(x−3)/[(x−5)(x+5)] and cancel the x−5 factor in the second numerator.
Factor (x−4)(x+2)/[(x+2)(x+3)] and cancel x−4 and one x+2.
An area is x²−9 square units and its width is x−3 units. Multiply the length (area/width) by 2x/(x+3). Assume x>3.
Length=(x²−9)/(x−3)=x+3; multiplying by 2x/(x+3) gives 2x. x>3 ensures positive dimensions and valid denominators.
For real a, ((x²−a²)/(x²−9))((x−3)/(x+a)) simplifies to (x−4)/(x+3). Find a and list exclusions for that value.
Factor x²−a²=(x−a)(x+a) and x²−9=(x−3)(x+3). The product becomes (x−a)/(x+3), so a=4; original denominators exclude x=±3 and x=−4.
Factor (x−1)(x+1)/[(x−1)(x−3)] times (x−3)(x+3)/[(x+1)(x+3)]. Every factor cancels, but all four original denominator zeros remain excluded.
tests: Numerators 5·2=10, denominators 3x; x cannot be zero.
Factor x²−25=(x−5)(x+5); cancel both factors, preserving both original restrictions.
Factor (x−5)(x+3)/[(x−3)(x+3)] times (x−3)/(x+5); cancel x−3 and x+3, leaving (x−5)/(x+5).
A student claims ((x²−16)/(x²−8x+16))((x−4)/(x+4))=1 for all real x. Correct the claim.
Factor (x−4)(x+4)/(x−4)² times (x−4)/(x+4)=1. Original denominators exclude x=4 and x=−4.
